title: Twelve Mac utilities. One native app.
excerpt: Recent files, time tracking, clipboard, battery care, screenshots, focus, workspaces and an anti-theft alarm. One native macOS app. No subscription.
content_html:
Public beta

The power of 12 premium
Mac apps. In one.

Recento Pro replaces the pile of single-purpose utilities on your Mac, recent files, time tracking, clipboard history, battery care, screenshots and recording, focus sessions, workspaces, a file shelf, an anti-theft alarm, menu bar stats and more, with one native app that runs quietly in the background.

macOS 14 or later · Apple Silicon & Intel · Beta 78

  • Native Swift, not Electron
  • Runs entirely on your Mac
  • No account required
  • No subscription

You have got one app for clipboard history. Another for screenshots. A third for battery limits. Each one wants menu bar space, login items, RAM, and its own $15.

They do not talk to each other. You paid for all of them separately. And half of them are Electron apps eating 300 MB to do something macOS could do in 5.

Recento Pro is all of it, written natively, in one place.

What's included

All twelve apps, in every download.

Recento Snap

Screenshots that look designed, not dumped.

  • Area, window, full-screen and scrolling capture, with a self-timer
  • Record the screen as video, or straight to GIF
  • Arrows, numbered steps, spotlight, pencil and blur, and blur sensitive text automatically
  • Copy text out of any screenshot
  • Pin a shot on screen, or drag it straight out of the corner preview

Everything Recento Snap does →

Recento Clipboard

Never lose something you copied again.

  • Searchable history of everything you have copied
  • Sort clips into colour-coded collections per project or client
  • Every clip shows the app it came from
  • Text, images, links, files and colours, shown as what they are

Everything Recento Clipboard does →

Recento Drop

A shelf for the drag you are in the middle of.

  • Floating shelves that hold files, links and text
  • Shake the cursor to summon one, or press Option Command D
  • Resize, convert, compress, stitch, read text out of images or make a PDF, right on the shelf
  • Several shelves at once, pinned or docked to a screen edge
  • A new shelf for every screenshot, straight from your screenshot folder

Everything Recento Drop does →

Recento Track

Find out where your day actually went.

  • Automatic time tracking, no timers to start
  • Per-app and per-website breakdown, down to the page
  • Rules file activity under a project on their own
  • Hourly rates, budgets and invoice PDFs for client work
  • Private iCloud sync between your Macs

Everything Recento Track does →

Recento Dial

Everything you reach for, one flick away.

  • A radial menu on a shortcut, right under your cursor
  • Pinned apps, files and links, plus your workspaces and shelves
  • Park it on screen as a small icon, and drag it anywhere
  • Hold the shortcut and flick, or click, scroll or use the arrow keys

Everything Recento Dial does →

Recento Workspaces

Your whole setup, restored in one click.

  • Save your apps, windows, browser tabs and folders as a workspace
  • Keeps each browser window separate, and remembers Dia and Chrome profiles
  • Restores only what is missing, never a second copy of a tab you already have
  • Hide everything else in one click to clear the desk

Everything Recento Workspaces does →

Recento Focus

Actually finish the thing.

  • Block distracting apps for a set session
  • Gentle mode lets you through after a pause. Hard Lock does not
  • Pomodoro cycles built in
  • Streaks and history so you can see progress

Everything Recento Focus does →

Recento Guard

Free

An alarm for the MacBook you left on the cafe table.

  • Arm it and walk away. Moving it, opening the lid, touching the keyboard or pulling the charger sets it off
  • A guarded screen warns anyone who looks before they touch
  • A siren you can hear across the room, or a milder sound for a quiet library
  • Photos and a short video of whoever touched it, sent to your iPhone through iMessage
  • Disarm with Touch ID

Everything Recento Guard does →

Recento Stats

Free

Your Mac at a glance, in the menu bar.

  • Startup disk space and how much is free
  • Where the power is going, across adapter, Mac and battery
  • Battery charge, health, cycles and temperature, with the percentage inside the battery
  • The apps using the most energy right now, and what is using the processor, quit either from the list
  • One icon, or Battery and Disk as icons of their own

Everything Recento Stats does →

Recento Battery

Make your battery last years, not months.

  • Charge limits and full health readout
  • Remind me to charge, an on-screen reminder that stays until you plug in
  • Tells you when a charger is plugged in but is not charging
  • Discharge while plugged in, paused automatically if the battery gets hot
  • Sailing Mode, Heat Protection and guided calibration

Everything Recento Battery does →

Recents MenuBar App

Everything you just worked on, one keystroke away.

  • Every file and folder you touched, ranked by recency
  • Filter by type, folder, or your own custom rules
  • Command 1 to 9 to reopen instantly from anywhere
  • A floating window you can pin over everything, and a right-click menu of your latest files

Everything Recents MenuBar App does →

Recento Utilities

Seven small tools you did not know you needed.

  • Shortcuts, free: a key of its own for any app, file, folder or link
  • Copy Paste, free: Ctrl C, Ctrl V and Ctrl X behave the way they do on Windows, leaving terminals and virtual machines alone
  • Stay Awake, with Bag Mode to keep a job running lid-shut, watching the processor temperature
  • Keyboard Lock, so you can wipe the keyboard down without typing into anything
  • Auto Eject installs a downloaded app for you, after a Gatekeeper check and always asking first
  • Better Wi-Fi moves you off a weak network when a stronger one is in range
  • Lid Fold, free: the screen frosts, dims and folds away as you close the lid. Seven styles

Everything Recento Utilities does →

ShortcutsCopy PasteStay AwakeKeyboard LockAuto EjectBetter Wi-FiLid Fold

Recento Battery

Remind me to charge

Notification banners disappear after four seconds. If you missed it, you missed it, and your Mac dies mid-sentence.

Recento Battery puts a reminder on screen and leaves it there until you plug in or dismiss it. It works even if you never granted notification permission, because it does not use notifications.

Recento Dial

Everything you reach for, one flick away

Press your shortcut anywhere. The dial opens under your cursor. Flick toward what you want and let go.

Other launchers open apps. This one opens entire workspaces, every app, tab and folder from a saved session, and your file shelves, in one flick. Or leave it parked on screen as a small, see-through icon until you need it.

Recento Snap

Screenshots worth sending

Capture, then drop it on a gradient with a soft shadow. Annotate it. Blur the parts nobody should see, automatically, using on-device text recognition.

Scrolling capture handles full pages. Recording handles the rest.

Recento Workspaces

Restore, not duplicate

Every other workspace restorer reopens the lot. If half your tabs are already open, you end up with two of each and close them by hand.

Recento Workspaces reads what is actually open first and opens only what is missing, comparing on a normalised URL, so a page that differs by www., a trailing slash or a tracking parameter still counts as already there. Each browser window comes back as its own window, in the right Dia or Chrome profile. When it cannot read a browser it says so and asks for access rather than reopening blind.

Recento Guard

An alarm for the laptop you walked away from

Leaving your MacBook on a cafe table while you order is a small act of faith.

Arm Recento Guard and walk away. If someone lifts it, opens the lid, touches the keyboard or unplugs the charger, it counts down a few seconds for you to disarm it, then sounds a siren, takes photos and a short video of whoever is there, and sends them to your iPhone. It uses your MacBook's own motion and lid sensors. It is free.

Honest limit: it cannot stop someone holding down the power button.

Where the dedicated apps still win

  • CleanShot X has cloud upload, shareable links and team features. We do not, everything stays on your Mac.
  • Paste syncs your clipboard across iPhone and iPad. We are Mac only.
  • Timing has deeper billing, invoicing and client reporting for people who bill by the hour.
  • iStat Menus monitors far more than we do, every sensor and network interface, with history. Recento Stats answers whether your disk is full, where your power is going and what is eating the battery, and stops there.
  • Menu bar managers like Bartender and Ice still do things we do not. On macOS 27 no third-party app can hide another app's icons any more, which is an Apple change rather than a gap either way.
  • Some of these have free equivalents. Amphetamine is free, Karabiner-Elements remaps keys for free, and Stats is a free menu bar monitor. If free is all you need, take free.

If you live in one of those workflows all day, buy the specialist. If you want twelve things done well without twelve purchases, that is us.

Build 1.0.33 Beta 78

What's new in the beta.

Beta 78

Recento installs your downloads for you

  • When a disk image finishes downloading, Recento offers to do the drag-to-Applications step: it copies the app inside into your Applications folder and ejects the image.
  • It asks every time and names the browser the download came from. Nothing is installed unless you click Install.
  • It checks the app with Gatekeeper first, never installs a .pkg on your behalf, and hands the image straight back if it holds more than one app or wants you to agree to a licence.
  • Replacing an app you already have sends the old version to the Trash, so you can get it back.
  • Off until you switch it on, in Recento Utilities, Auto Eject.
  • Fix: the Battery Almost Full notice no longer repeats while the battery sits near the top.

Beta 77

One shelf on a shake, and a deeper Stats dropdown

  • Recento Drop: shaking the cursor mid-drag used to bring back every shelf at once. You now get one empty shelf where you are about to drop, with a setting for the old behaviour.
  • Recento Drop also gained Close All and Delete All Shelves.
  • Recento Stats: the dropdown opens over full-screen apps, has a Top Processes tab with a quit button on hover, and draws the charge percentage inside the battery with the time remaining underneath.
  • Auto Eject now ejects installer images that were already mounted before Recento started.
  • Recento Snap: the on-screen instructions no longer end up in a scrolling screenshot, and zoomed-in detail is sharper.
  • Better Wi-Fi says when macOS will not reveal nearby network names, instead of showing an empty list.
  • Two crashes while the menu bar was being rearranged, fixed.

Recently, in the betas before these

Two new apps, and two new free tools

  • Recento Stats and Recento Guard are both new apps. Guard is a free anti-theft alarm for your MacBook.
  • Lid Fold and Copy Paste, two new free tools in Recento Utilities.
  • Bag Mode now watches the processor temperature rather than the battery's, and tells you when it had to put the Mac to sleep.
  • Recento Workspaces saves and restores each browser window separately, with its Dia or Chrome profile, and no longer reopens tabs you already had open.
  • Recento Snap: delete a capture and the saved copy goes to the Trash with it. Esc backs out one step at a time, and annotations keep working when you zoom.
  • Updates install with one click, and there is a Debug Log you can switch on and paste into a bug report.

Your data never leaves your Mac.

Recento tracks what you do so it can show it back to you. That information stays on your machine. There is no server, no account, no sync we can read, and no analytics on your file names or screen contents.

  • No account required. Download and use it.
  • No telemetry on your content, ever.
  • Anonymous crash diagnostics are opt-in, and off unless you turn them on.
  • Recento Track's sync is optional and goes through your own iCloud account, which we cannot read.
  • Recento Guard's photos and video stay on your Mac. If you turn on alerts they go from your Messages app to your own iPhone, never through us.
  • Notarised by Apple. Signed with a Developer ID.
  • macOS permissions are requested only when an app needs one, and we tell you exactly which app and why.

Frequently asked questions

Is this a subscription?

Only if you want it to be. The lifetime licence is one payment of $99, yours forever, with all future updates included. There is also a monthly plan at $9.99 with a 2 day free trial, for anyone who would rather not pay up front.

Where do I download it?

Always the latest beta, from the download button on this page. Open the file and drag Recento Pro into Applications.

Does the free version expire?

No. It is not a trial. It stays free and functional for as long as you want.

What macOS do I need?

macOS 14 (Sonoma) or later. Apple Silicon and Intel are both supported.

Can I use it on more than one Mac?

Yes. The licence covers your personal Macs.

Why does it need Accessibility, Screen Recording or Camera permission?

Accessibility lets Recento see which app is frontmost, which is what time tracking, focus blocking, restoring workspaces and the menu bar rely on. Screen Recording is what macOS requires of any app that captures the screen, so Snap needs it. Camera is only for Recento Guard's photo and video evidence, and only if you switch that on. None is used for anything else, and all are optional. The rest of the app works without them.

Does it slow my Mac down?

It is native Swift, not Electron. It is a menu bar app that idles most of the time, and every app can be switched off in the launcher.

Which Macs does Lid Fold work on?

Macs with a lid angle sensor: MacBook Air M2 and later, and most 14 inch and 16 inch MacBook Pro. Not the M1 MacBook Air or the 13 inch MacBook Pro.

macOS 26.4 added a battery charge limit. Do I still need Recento Battery?

Apple's built-in limit stops at 80% and does nothing else. Recento Battery adds Sailing Mode, Heat Protection, guided calibration, scheduling, per-app power impact and the persistent charge reminder. On the newest macOS builds Apple's firmware handles the limit itself, and Recento defers to it rather than fighting it.

Do I have to go looking for updates?

No. Recento checks for updates and downloads them in the background, then asks you to restart when one is ready.

If Recento launches at login, do I have to open each app for it to work?

No, and this is the part people expect to be true and it is not. Every enabled app starts working the moment Recento does: Track records, Battery holds your charge limit, Drop watches for the shake gesture, all with nothing on screen. Opening a window only shows you what it has been doing. If you want certain pages up when you sit down, pick them in Settings.

What happens when the beta ends?

Your licence keeps working. Pre-launch buyers keep the lifetime licence at the price they paid.

Can I get a refund?

Yes, 30 days, no argument.

Start with the free beta, every app is included. Upgrade when you hit a limit that matters to you.
